lenses.mechanism_summary: The mechanism check's 8-of-15 'kpf move' count is mostly a labeling effect plus one real gap. Read by whole turn, koh's 15 reached Swablu/Eevee turns are 7 kp3-like, 7 kpf-like, 1 other. Fix A did its job on Swablu: koh never makes kpf's Igglybuff->bare-Swablu retreat at turn T (0 of 18 rows; kpf does it in 8). What is left is (a) four Igglybuff->Eevee retreats at the first turn (Igglybuff openers, Zone P onto Eevee, Stampede instead of Sleepy Lullaby), (b) one Eevee->Swablu, (c) two feed-the-Active-Swablu-and-Sing turns that are Dustin's neutral 'pure form', and (d) one move-order artifact. A cannot gate Eevee by construction: Eevee's yardstick is Espeon [P] (one Energy), Eevee[P] reads 1.0 in kog and kp3 already, and A floors at that unprojected reading; Boosted Evolution is not the reason, since Igglybuff opened in all four and koh Stampedes rather than evolving. At scale (Altaria v Blaziken and v Lucario, 1000 deals of full watch-only dumps, trace lengths matching the official rows) the Eevee[P]+Stampede line is not koh-specific: koh 22 games, kog 25, and the paired outcomes by retreat line are flat. The measurable koh-vs-kog difference is elsewhere: more idle turns (+0.31 per game, z ~10), fewer Sleepy Lullabies (-0.14), more Zone Energy into the Active Darkrai/Mega Altaria ex, more turns with an unready main attacker in front. That is the tempo trade (main attacker moved up early, cheap attack dropped) that R' keeps by design, with fix B's payment test (cost <= Energy held, so bench credit is denied behind Darkrai, retreat 2) as one plausible reason it survives for Altaria. Its cost shows in the Lucario cell (-4.8 +/- 3.8), not in Blaziken (+1.0 +/- 4.6). The 23-row outcomes (kp3 19, kpf 4, koh 12 of 23) are selection-driven and do not test koh.
candidate_fix_ideas: Change the reading, not the player: score the mechanism check by whole-turn end board (or by 'retreat into an unevolved Basic'), not by the first differing action. On that unit, A holds for Swablu (0 of 8 kpf-style retreats) and the 0.40 line becomes 0.47; the crossing is then about Eevee and the pure-form rows, and only 4-5 rows (72020028, 72020187, 72030010, 72060061, 72040056) carry it. No player change is indicated by the Swablu/Eevee slice itself.

Drop A's floor at the unprojected reading whenever steps > 0 (reading = the evolution-aware projected value only), so Eevee[P] with no Espeon on the board reads 0 rather than 1.0. No new constant. Would change the 4 Igglybuff->Eevee rows and 72040056; would NOT change the 2 Swablu-Sing rows (72000083, 72030147), 72000046, the hide row 72050131, or the Darkrai rows. It also changes Swablu[PP] (1.0 -> 0.5) and kog's own Eevee reading, and kog does the same Stampede line at a similar rate, so expected deck value is small; needs the full 45 cells.

Let B's reach test count the Energy the Active will hold after next turn's Zone attach (or drop the payment test when the Active's retreat cost exceeds its Energy, i.e. Darkrai in front), so a benched Mega Altaria ex behind an unready Darkrai still gets the Zone credit and the Active-feeding preference weakens. No new constant. Would change the Darkrai(Active)-vs-Mega(bench) attach positions (72020043 T4, 72020052 T3, 72020173 T3, 72020177 T3; n=31 in 1000 deals) and possibly 72000065 and the Igglybuff->Darkrai retreats (0.032 vs 0.002 per game). Conflicts with Dustin's Q10 note that motivated the payment test (Vespiquen), so check Vespiquen's forward swaps.

Fix the clock's threat pick (older than R, shared with kp3/kog, DIAGNOSIS 'Not addressed'): choose the threat by fewest turns to win (missing Energy + hits needed) instead of fewest missing Energy then most damage, so a free 10-damage chip stops outranking a real attacker one Energy short. Removes the reason the clock rewards moving an attacker up a turn early, i.e. the tempo trade behind the +0.31 idle turns per game. No new constant, but it changes the base for every deck, so it is a separate candidate, not a koh amendment. Rows it would change: the unready-main-attacker turns (idle-turn family, Lucario cell), 72020097 and 72000065 swaps; likely not the Eevee Stampede rows.

Before any of these, dump the evaluator's terms (readiness, both clocks, safety) for the chosen and the rejected leaf at six boards where koh differs from kog: 72020187 T2 and 72020028 T2 (Igglybuff->Eevee Stampede), 72030147 T2 and 72000083 T2 (feed Active Swablu and Sing), 72020043 T4 (Darkrai Active vs bench Mega), 72050131 T4 (bare Swablu in front, Mega[PP] benched). That names the flipping term without guessing; my code reading says readiness is equal to kog's in the Eevee/Swablu leaves, so the clock/R terms should be doing the work.

lenses.mechanism_summary: koh differs from kog in 83% of Altaria's deals (Altaria's own decision each time, identical board at the split, openings never differ), but 72% of those games end the same way; the whole own-side loss is a net 46 deals in 3,500 (-1.33 +/- 1.61 points over the 7 traced cells; -4.8 +/- 3.8 in the Lucario cell). Fix A did what it was built to do: kpf's Swablu-in-front rows (12/2) are gone (16/15), the Igglybuff retreat rows are neutral (36/31), and koh's retreats into Eevee, which the mechanism check flagged, are outcome-neutral in fresh deals (162 deals, 27/24, -0.09 +/- 0.40 points; turn-1 retreat-and-evolve through Boosted Evolution 21/21). What is left is spread over three weaker patterns. (1) Zone Energy goes to the Active where kog builds the Bench, the largest net piece (82/54 vs 33/33 the other way, about -0.8 of -1.33 points); in the cleanest same-board decision, kog feeds a just-evolved benched Mega Altaria ex and koh feeds the Active Darkrai (79 games, 19/5), which fix A cannot touch (Darkrai does not evolve) and the readiness score still credits the Active only. (2) koh attacks less (567 turns where only kog attacks vs 59 the other way); this costs points only in Lucario (18/3, -3.0 of -4.8), where a Sleepy Lullaby is lost to an early forward swap or to feeding a bench Pokemon behind a 0-Energy Espeon or Darkrai. (3) Eevee: koh evolves and leaves Eevee in front less often than kog, but when the two arms disagree on the Eevee->Espeon evolution kog is the one that made it in 59 turns (23/6, all 7 cells), largely a draw-order difference (koh declines a held Espeon in only 7 of 167 identical-board cases), and a bare Eevee left in front costs whoever does it, so its net is about zero (-0.06 for Eevee in front, -0.34 for the evolution timing). The harm is skewed late: divergences at turn 4 or later carry -0.88 of the -1.33. The Swablu/Eevee crossing in the mechanism check is really the Eevee retreat rows (4 of 4 reproduced) and is not where points are lost; Eevee's Espeon costs one Energy, so an Eevee holding one P reads 1.0 on kp3's unprojected floor and A's step cannot lower it. All the causal links to R' above are hypotheses read from the boards; the patterns are found after looking and the statistics are weak.
candidate_fix_ideas: Give fix B's recipient rule to the readiness score as well as the clock: when R' credits next turn's Zone Energy in the Active's readiness reading, take the larger of the Active's reading and each benched Pokemon's reading that B's own reachability test (bench_can_reach_active) says can be in front next turn, so a benched Mega Altaria ex is credited like the Active Darkrai. It uses an existing gate and adds no constant, and it never reads below R'. It would change: the Zone-to-Active rows (82/54 vs 33/33), the clean 79-game Mega Altaria ex-on-Bench vs Darkrai-in-front decision (19/5), 'pure feed-the-Active' (52/36), 'feeding Darkrai' (81/56) and Lucario's Zone-target piece (about -1.4 of -4.8). It should leave Swablu-front rows, Rayquaza (the Active stays a recipient) and Lucario's hides alone. Risk: more forward swaps, the original Lucario/Vespiquen problem, if the reachability test is loose.

Withhold R''s next-turn credit from a leaf where the Active could have paid for an attack this turn and did not: at a leaf after the owner's turn, credit the projection only if an attack was used or none was payable, using energy_missing on the Active's current Energy. No new number. It would change the attack-skip rows (567 turns kog-only v 59; Lucario 18/3, -3.0 of -4.8), the 0-Energy-Espeon rows and the turn-1 Igglybuff->Eevee->Espeon Lullaby skip (98 turns, neutral, so expect little there). It keeps the credit exactly where Rayquaza's gain lives (after Mega Burst or Scorching Interruption the attack was used). Risk: it acts on every deck's turn and would need the full 45 cells.

Charge A's evolution step on the unprojected (kp3) floor too, but only when the evolution card is not in hand (waive it when the card is in hand, which covers Eevee's Boosted Evolution): a Basic that cannot become its yardstick card this turn stops reading as ready on Energy alone. Same one-step-per-missing-Energy rule, same hand list the readiness score already reads. It would change the 'unevolved Swablu/Eevee left in front' rows (koh-only 33/13, net -0.43) and Lucario's bare-Riolu rows, and would not touch Rayquaza. Expect little for Altaria: Eevee-in-front nets -0.06 because kog leaves it in front more often than koh, and this is a kp3-level change that also moves kog, so the koh-minus-kog gap may barely move.

Do not register any of these on Altaria's evidence alone. Every piece is under 1 point over the deck and cannot be resolved at 500 deals per cell; the rows above support choosing which of the three to test, not proving one. If one is built, judge it on the Zone-target and attack-skip rows first (both have same-board decision subsets: Zone 79 games, 19/5; Lucario skip 81 turns, 18/3), and read the Eevee->Espeon timing rows only with hand contents in the dump.

What koh does on Eevee is R itself, through the clock: kp3's threat pick (fewest missing Energy first, value_functions.rs:1188) lets a free 10-damage Igglybuff or an unpowered benched Eevee stand in for the real attacker (our win clock reads 20-30 turns), while R projects Energy onto the Active and the min over projected clocks (6-8 turns). On the actor's first turn Boosted Evolution (move_generation/mod.rs:199-209, unread by the evaluator) lets the depth-3 search reach 'draw, Retreat into Eevee, evolve to Espeon' as a mid-turn leaf that R values +2000 above what kp3 sees; Retreat-first and draw-first reach the same leaf, tie exactly, and the tie goes to Retreat (last max, JSON sort order), before the draw is known and on a sampled (optimistic) Espeon draw that hit 0 of 3 in the real rows. The other Eevee/Swablu kpf-moves are separate R effects: Sabrina lines lose value because R projects Energy onto the opponent's promoted Active (2 rows), the unpowered-Eevee clock hijack disappears (2 rows), and a Swablu-with-P Active gets a large projected clock credit (1 row). Fix B does nothing for Eevee (kphb equals kpf on all six), koa's switch A is setup-only and only explains 2 of the 3 unreached rows (kog/koh open Eevee 387 v 137). A smoothed threat pick applied to both bots raises koh-versus-base agreement from 73 to 139 of 200 rows, so most of the divergence is the older pick rule interacting with R, not A or B.

**Diagnosis: why koh plays Altaria worse (synthesizer, Sept 28 night)**

Terms: R is kpf's projection, where next turn's Zone Energy is credited to the Active. A makes an evolution step count as a missing Energy. B lets the Zone Energy be credited to a benched Pokémon that can reach the Active. koh = kog + R + A + B.

**Short answer**
1. The "crossed" Swablu/Eevee line is mostly a reading problem. A works on Swablu and cannot act on Eevee, and the Eevee lines don't cost points.
2. koh's Altaria deficit is small and spread over three pieces. Over the 7 traced cells it is −1.33 ± 1.61, and the READING's deck figure is −1.8 ± 1.4. No single piece is significant on its own.
3. Only one piece has a mechanism I could pin down and repair with no collateral change on the registered slices. That is B's retreat-payment test (fix 1 below).
4. Altaria's evidence alone does not justify changing the player.

**What I checked (verified by rerunning or reading)**
- **Mechanism check:** 6 kp3-move / 8 kpf-move / 1 other, 15 of 18 rows reached. Read by whole turn it is 7 / 7 / 1 (I reran `classify_rows.py`).
